item.title: Looking back at local news from the archives
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Looking back at local news from the archives
We are looking back at local stories from the archives this week. In 1994, staff from the Methwold firm Howard Long International raised £2,600 for the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn. The money, collected through a sponsored three-legged pub crawl, was used to furnish a quiet room near the accident and emergency department.
Meanwhile, in 2001, protestors gathered outside RAF Feltwell for a peaceful vigil. Around 20 people took part in the demonstration, which was part of a global movement opposing the militarisation of space and the American National Missile Defence plans. The event also served as a response to the conflict in Afghanistan.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Police investigation continues into Wisbech murder
Police inquiries are ongoing following the death of 37-year-old Atis Bleive in Wisbech. Officers were called to a property on Osborne Road at approximately 4pm on January 19, where Mr Bleive was pronounced dead at the scene. A post-mortem examination confirmed he died from a stab wound to the abdomen.
Two local people were arrested on suspicion of murder. A 41-year-old man was released under investigation, while a 45-year-old woman remains on bail until December 29. Detectives have confirmed that the investigation into the circumstances surrounding the death is continuing.

item.title: West Norfolk Council declines to detail swimming pool planning costs
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
West Norfolk Council declines to detail swimming pool planning costs
West Norfolk Council has declined a request to provide a breakdown of the £845,609 spent on planning a new swimming pool at Lynnsport. The local authority stated that the information is commercially sensitive and that releasing details could prejudice future contract negotiations.
The proposed £23 million facility is intended to replace the existing St James Swimming Pool. Council leader Alistair Beales defended the expenditure, noting that planning in a flood zone involves uncertain ground conditions. While the council approved the planning budget last month, officials emphasised that the project remains in the development phase. Previous attempts to relocate the pool to Lynnsport were abandoned after feasibility studies suggested costs could exceed £45 million.

item.title: Police appeal following serious collision in Sawtry
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Police appeal following serious collision in Sawtry
Police are appealing for witnesses after a serious collision between a lorry and a motorbike in Sawtry yesterday. The incident occurred at approximately 12:50pm on the B1043 Old North Road, involving a red Volvo HGV and a black Kawasaki motorbike. The motorcyclist, a 23-year-old man from Yaxley, was taken to Addenbrooke’s Hospital with life-threatening injuries.
The lorry driver, a 76-year-old man from Wisbech, was arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by careless driving and has been released on bail until January 4. Officers are urging anyone with information or dashcam footage to contact the police via their website or by calling 101, quoting reference 35/77423/26.

Future of West Lynn’s Freebridge Farm site remains uncertain
The Freebridge Farm restaurant in West Lynn could potentially reopen following a national deal involving its parent company, Whitbread PLC. The site on Clenchwarton Road closed last month as part of a wider move to reduce the number of Brewers Fayre and Beefeater locations across the UK.
Two hospitality firms, Common Table Group and Queensway Inns, have now acquired over 100 branches between them. While it is not yet confirmed if the West Lynn site is included in this purchase, the new owners plan to begin reopening locations as early as next month. The move is expected to create 1,400 jobs across the country.

Witnesses sought following hit-and-run in King’s Lynn
Norfolk Police are appealing for information after a hit-and-run incident in King’s Lynn on Sunday evening. At approximately 10:50pm, a dark-coloured 4x4 collided with a parked silver Suzuki Swift on Southgate Street, causing significant damage to the vehicle. Doorbell footage captured the collision, and officers are now working to identify the driver involved.
Anyone who witnessed the incident or possesses relevant dashcam footage is urged to contact Norfolk Police. You can assist the investigation by calling 01603 276220 or emailing RoadCollisionsSupportTeam@Suffolk.police.uk, quoting reference URN 1825752. Alternatively, information can be provided anonymously to Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.
